label: conj:qdifference-kernel-prolongation-symbol
title: The q-difference kernel R is the jet-prolongation symbol, carried by the binding q-lift module
html:
Conjecture (the q-difference kernel is the prolongation symbol).

The q-difference kernel R(q,x) of the binding generating function (prop:binding-genfun-qdifference) is the symbol of the jet-prolongation operator J^{n}E\to J^{n+1}E of the Seiberg--Witten connection (prop:mi-sw-abelianisation).

Its carrier is the rank-2 q-difference module \mathcal{K} of the binding q-lift recurrence

[m+2]_q\,b_{m+2} \;=\; b_{m+1} + b_m ,

equivalently, writing x=q^{m} and \sigma:x\mapsto qx, the module of

L_{\mathcal{K}} \;=\; (q^{2}x-1)\,\sigma^{2}\;-\;(q-1)\,\sigma\;-\;(q-1).

At x=\infty the Newton polygon of L_{\mathcal{K}} has the single slope \tfrac12 with multiplicity 2: \mathcal{K} is pure isoclinic of slope \tfrac12.

Scope note. This conjecture previously continued "— equivalently, the monodromy/Stokes data of the prolonged SW connection at the branch-point poles of \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)}", identifying \mathcal{K} with the Stokes carrier of the resurgent colored-Jones series of [garoufalidis-gu-marino2021]. That equivalence is false as an identification of q-difference modules, and the clause has been removed. The Stokes carrier is the module \mathcal{G} of y_{m+2}-(2-q^{m+1})\,y_{m+1}+y_m=0, whose Newton polygon at x=\infty has the two slopes \{-1,+1\}; \mathcal{K}'s is \{\tfrac12,\tfrac12\}. Since the Newton polygon is a module invariant and its slope multiset is preserved by every gauge transformation ([rsz2013] Thm 2.2.1(i), Thm 2.2.4), no isomorphism of q-difference modules \mathcal{K}\cong\mathcal{G} exists. The surviving — and genuinely non-trivial — relationship between the two is stated separately as conj:c1-ggm-bar-parity-faces.

Two consequences follow:

  1. R is structurally fixed, not fitted. The prolongation operator is a single fibre-level object; its symbol is read off the connection, not tuned to reproduce the terms. This is forced by the precision-floor obstruction (the c_k information bound makes term data unable to fix R beyond low order), and it is the same fibre-level / root-of-unity singularity structure that governs the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta ladder.
  2. It closes the binding program. Given R, the recurrence of prop:binding-genfun-qdifference determines every body term from the deuteron base case (fixing the \rho\cdot A growth law), which is precisely the per-term mass identity. Feeding it into thm:binding-closure-conditional discharges its one conditional input, promoting conj:binding-manybody-eq-jet-filtration from conditional to unconditional.

This conjecture is therefore the single remaining input to the binding closure: the residue form, the body-order = jet-degree coincidence, and the recurrence machinery are all proved; only the identification of R with the prolongation symbol remains. It is stated here as a precise, falsifiable structural claim — to be derived from the prolonged connection's local monodromy, not fitted numerically.

Scope note (2026-08-26) — \mathcal{K} is irreducible, so consequence 2 is wrong by exactly one initial condition. The pure-isoclinic slope-\tfrac12 statement above has a consequence the conjecture did not draw. A rank-1 q-difference module over \mathbb{Q}(q)(x) has integer slope, and Newton slopes are additive on sub- and quotient modules — the same invariant, and the same citation ([rsz2013] Thm 2.2.1(i), Thm 2.2.4), that the scope note above uses to separate \mathcal{K} from \mathcal{G}. Since \{\tfrac12,\tfrac12\} contains no integer, \mathcal{K} has no rank-1 sub- or quotient module: it is irreducible. Equivalently, and provable without any module theory, the associated q-Riccati (q^2x-1)a(qx)a(x) - (q-1)a(x) - (q-1) = 0 has no solution in K(x), because the three terms of its cleared form have degrees 1+2p, p+u, 2u and the odd/even parity of the outer two forces the maximum to be attained exactly once. Sorry-free in QOU.Mass.BindingScalarKernelParityExclusion; corroborated by the van der Put--Reversat classification [vanderput-reversat2007, vanderput2006] of pure modules of non-integral slope d/r — the normal form E(r,d,b) in Bugeaud's notation [bugeaud2011] — which is irreducible when the rank equals r; here r = 2 = \mathrm{rank}\mathcal{K}.

Two revisions follow.

  1. Consequence 1 is unchanged but must be read in rank 2. The prolongation symbol of a rank-2 carrier is a 2\times2 matrix A(q,x) acting on (G,\sigma G), not a scalar R(q,x). The claim that the symbol is structurally fixed rather than fitted is untouched; only its shape changes. This is the natural reading of the Dirac-type \tau-image asserted in prop:binding-genfun-qdifference, since a Dirac operator is first-order on a two-component object.
  2. Consequence 2 is falsified as stated. "Given R, the recurrence determines every body term from the deuteron base case" is wrong by exactly one initial condition: a rank-2 module needs two. The n=2 deuteron term alone does not close the recursion; the genuine three-body n=3 term is independently required, and is not fixed by the existing anchors.

This narrows rather than refutes the conjecture: the identification of the kernel with the prolongation symbol remains open and remains the single structural input, but it must be sought as a rank-2 symbol, and the closure it would deliver needs a second base case.

Scope note (2026-09-03) — what the prolongation operator must look like on the ramified chart, before it is constructed. The classical lift d/dz is excluded (prop:sw-classical-jet-exactness), and the residue that a period needs vanishes for it locally, at every branch point, because at z = z_c + t^2 the operator d/dz = (1/2t)\,d/dt reads the t^{-2} residue slot from the constant term with multiplier (-2)+2 = 0. That observation generalises exactly. On the coefficient model f:\mathbb{Z}\to R of a local Laurent expansion, every derivative-like operator is a shift operator (S_{k,c}f)(e) = c(e)\,f(e+k) — a pair (shift k, multiplier c), which is its symbol on the punctured t-disk, and symbols compose by adding shifts and multiplying multipliers along the shift. Two exact facts then constrain any single-shift candidate D_q (QOU.Mathlib.RamifiedShiftCalculus, sorry-free over a generic commutative ring):

  1. Residue. If D_q annihilates constants, c(-k) = 0 — as every derivative does: d/dz, its q-deformation [e+2]_q in either q-integer convention, the Jackson operator [e+1]_q in the local coordinate, all because [0]_q = 0 — then for shift k \in \{1, 2\} the residue slot is dead at every jet level on a power-series seed such as the colour-cubic branch. No derivative-like prolongation of shift 1 or 2 can produce the binding period. A residue needs a component with c(-k) \neq 0: a genuine zeroth-order term, which in rank 2 is the connection-matrix datum the previous note already places the symbol in.
  2. Parity. An even shift commutes with the covering monodromy t \mapsto -t; an odd shift anti-commutes, so its jet tower's monodromy eigenvalue alternates as (-1)^n — the Door-v residual of conj:c1-ggm-bar-parity-faces. Carrying that residual needs an odd shift.

So D_q must have an odd shift and a non-derivative component. Both conditions are derived from the local geometry of \Sigma and the two measured target properties, never from the kernel's coefficients — the anti-fit obligation is respected. D_q is not constructed here; the class is narrowed, which is what the scoping audit's walls W1–W2 asked for first.

The sum case does not behave as the single-shift case suggests. For a finite sum \sum_k c_k\sigma^k the residue slot of the n-th jet is a sum over words, and the word (shift 1, then shift 2) reads t^{-2} from t^{-1} and t^{-1} from t^{+1}, never landing on the constant slot where a derivative's multiplier vanishes. So two derivative-like terms of shifts 1 and 2 — classical d/dt + (1/t)\,d/dt, or Jackson [e+1]_q with [e+2]_q — do reach the residue slot: at level n+2 it is c_1(-2)\,c_2(-1) times the t^{1} coefficient of the level-n jet, weight -1 in both cases (QOU.Mathlib.RamifiedShiftCalculusSum, sorry-free). The non-derivative clause is therefore a single-shift statement. What restores it for sums is the residual: an operator with even part E and odd part O satisfies \mathrm{mono}(Df) = E(\mathrm{mono}\,f) - O(\mathrm{mono}\,f), and a tower carrying the full (-1)^n alternation is generated by O alone with E annihilating every level — after which the single-shift prune kills the residue again. For derivative-like sums of shifts \le 2 the residue and the residual are mutually exclusive level by level: alternation demanded from a level n_0 on kills the residue from level n_0+2 on and leaves levels 2,\dots,n_0+1 alive (twoOp_residual_from_level_kills_residue_beyond). The distinction matters, because the Door-v alternation of the carrier \mathcal{G} in conj:c1-ggm-bar-parity-faces cannot hold at every level — while 2-q^{m+1}>0 no solution flips at two consecutive pairs (QOU.Mass.GGMAlternationOnset), so at the substrate value the alternation is absent for m \le 5 and persistent only from m \approx 11 on. The conclusion above therefore stands for sums only above that window; at the low body orders a mixed-shift D_q built from derivatives alone remains admissible by the two target properties, and the non-derivative clause is not forced by them there.

The kernel is a recurrence across jet levels, and on that axis it forces the non-derivative clause too. In L_{\mathcal{K}} the variable is x = q^{m} with m the body order, which prop:sw-period-residue-sum identifies with the jet degree; so \sigma is the step from one jet level to the next, and L_{\mathcal{K}} is the second-order recurrence that the level-indexed residues r_{n} = (D_{q}^{n}X)_{t^{-2}} of the prolongation tower must satisfy — never D_{q} itself, which is first-order in the level. On a power-series seed r_{0} = 0 for every operator, so the residue tower cannot coincide with a carrier whose first term is nonzero (the involution-number carrier has b_{0} = b_{1} = 1): the recurrence is demanded from a level on, and a level-n_{0} C1 sequence is fixed by its two values at n_{0} and n_{0}+1 — the two base cases of the scope note above. For the admissible two-term operator r_{1} = c_{2}(-2)\,a_{0}, the branch value read through the shift-2 weight at the residue slot; a derivative-like shift-2 term has c_{2}(-2) = 0, so r_{0} = r_{1} = 0 and a C1 residue tower from level 0 is identically zero. For a derivative-only tower the recurrence from level 2 is equivalent to the index-shifted recurrence [m+4]_{q}\,s_{m+2} = s_{m+1} + s_{m} on the tower's t^{1}-coefficients s_{m} = (D_{q}^{m}X)_{t^{1}}, since r_{m+2} = c_{1}(-2)c_{2}(-1)\,s_{m}; each level's constraint reaches one new seed coefficient and none of them reads the branch value a_{0} (QOU.Mass.C1KernelLevelReading, sorry-free, q not a root of unity). On the actual seed — the branch-point expansion of the colour cubic at its simple ramification point — neither the Jackson nor the q-derivative tower, in either q-integer convention and on either sheet, satisfies that recurrence at any tested q: the defect is of order one relative to the residues themselves, not a precision artefact. And with the weights left free, each level introduces at least four new weight values against one constraint, so the recurrence constrains nothing until the weights are supplied by the geometry. Both statements are scope-(a): they concern these two candidates on this seed, and the two-term derivative-only class, respectively. The weights cannot be supplied by a q-connection on the base either: the colour cubic is irreducible over K(z) for every field K of characteristic zero (QOU.Mass.ColorCubicIrreducible, sorry-free), so no sheet is a rational function of z; each sheet is algebraic, hence D-finite; and a rational rank-3 q-difference system in z \mapsto \lambda z with the sheets as solutions would make a sheet q-holonomic, which together with D-finiteness forces rationality (Bézivin, Ramis; Schäfke–Singer). So a rational q-connection on the z-line with the sheets as flat sections does not exist — scope (b), the cited theorem being the invariant. Localising at the ramification point does not evade this. In the local coordinate t, with z = z_{c} + t^{2}, the sheets are power series algebraic over K(t) and so still D-finite; and they are still not rational, because t^{2} = z - z_{c} makes K(t)/K(z) quadratic while an irreducible cubic has no root of degree at most two (QOU.Mass.IrreducibleCubicNoQuadraticRoot, sorry-free). The same theorem therefore excludes the local q-dilation as well, and what survives is an operator whose coefficients are not rational in a coordinate, or one defined on the curve rather than on a coordinate line.

Two earlier readings of the same kernel took \sigma to be a shift in the t-exponent of a single jet — the unit t-shift with x = q^{e}, or the t-shift by two on the double cover. That is the special case in which the level and the exponent lock, r_{n} = c^{n}a_{n-2} for a constant-weight pure shift-1 tower, not the conjecture's reading. What was proved there stands as mathematics about those t-operators: neither can be written as a sum of derivative-like terms, because each carries a zeroth-order term -(q-1) that does not annihilate the constant seed (QOU.Mass.C1KernelAsShiftSum), and neither can carry the (-1)^{m} alternation of the preceding note on a nonzero tower — on the double cover because a monodromy-commuting operator transports the character unchanged, under the unit shift because the even part would have to annihilate both a jet and its odd image, and those two recurrences differ by q^{e+1}(q-1)Y_{e+2} (QOU.Mass.C1KernelDictionaryParity). Read on the correct axis those facts say nothing about D_{q}, and the "\sigma \leftrightarrow t-shift dictionary" they posed as wall W2 is not a question the conjecture asks.

Scope note (2026-09-05) — an operator on the curve does not evade the exclusion either, when its base map is a dilation. The two preceding exclusions constrain the coefficient field, so an operator living on \Sigma rather than on a coordinate line is not reached by them. It is reached by the branch locus. An automorphism of \Sigma covering the base dilation z \mapsto \lambda z is an isomorphism of coverings up to that base automorphism, so it carries ramification points to ramification points and therefore permutes the six finite branch points — the zeros of the branch sextic D(z) = 16z^{6} + 24z^{5} + 35z^{4} + 50z^{3} + 35z^{2} + 24z + 16, which is squarefree with D(0) = 16 \neq 0. Equal root multisets means D(\lambda z) = c\,D(z), and then two coefficients settle it: the constant term gives 16 = 16c, so c = 1, and the linear term gives 24\lambda = 24, so \lambda = 1 (QOU.Mass.DilationBranchLocusRigidity, sorry-free, generic characteristic-zero field). Only the identity dilation lifts to \Sigma, for every \lambda and at every q — scope (b), the invariant being the sextic's own coefficients rather than a cited analytic theorem, so this covers the root-of-unity case that the rationality theorem does not. The substrate asks for \lambda = q_{0}^{2} \approx 1.2321, which is excluded both by that identity and by the weaker bound \lambda^{6} = 1 that the product of the roots alone would give. This does not touch a q-difference operator whose base map is not a dilation, nor the fibre monodromy route, which acts on the fibre and is untouched by any statement about maps of the z-line.
